eg: Server and domain isolation are built from these rules. A connection security rule on its own does not allow traffic through the firewall, and disabling the firewall also removes the IPsec connection security capability.

term: Microsoft Entra Password Protection for AD DS
def: Enforces the global banned-password list plus a per-tenant custom list on on-premises password changes. A Password Protection proxy service on a domain-joined member server (never a DC) relays policy requests to Microsoft Entra ID, and the DC agent installed on each domain controller downloads the policy, stores it in SYSVOL, and validates changes through a password filter. DCs never contact the internet, clear-text passwords never leave the DC, and the policy is enforced only on DCs that run the agent.
eg: Incremental deployment is supported but password changes sent to a DC without the agent are not checked, so aim for full coverage. The DC agent checks for a newer policy hourly and does not listen on a network port.

term: Securing privileged AD groups and domain controllers
def: Limit membership of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, and Schema Admins to the few people who need them (Schema Admins can stay empty until a schema change), protect privileged accounts as Protected Users, and administer DCs only from hardened admin workstations. DCs should run few roles, ideally on Server Core, with restricted interactive and remote logon, no internet browsing, and a locked-down firewall. The AdminSDHolder process re-applies a protected ACL to privileged accounts about every 60 minutes.
eg: Restricting who can log on to DCs shrinks the credential-theft surface, since anything that logs on to a DC can leave reusable credentials there. Tiered administration keeps domain admin credentials off lower-tier servers.

def: Delegation grants a group a narrow set of permissions over a scope, usually an OU, instead of membership in a highly privileged group. The Delegation of Control Wizard assigns common tasks (reset user passwords, manage group membership, create or delete users) on the chosen OU, and the result is an access control entry on the OU. This applies least privilege so, for example, help desk staff can reset passwords only for one department's users.
eg: Delegate to groups, not individuals, keep the delegated scope as small as practical, and review it periodically. Do not confuse AD delegation with Kerberos delegation, which lets a service act on a user's behalf.

term: Performance Monitor and Data Collector Sets
def: Performance Monitor displays real-time or logged performance counters (like CPU, memory, disk queue length). A Data Collector Set groups counters, trace data, and configuration into a single, reusable, schedulable collection job, so the same set of metrics can be captured consistently over time rather than configured freshly each time.
eg: A Data Collector Set can be configured to trigger an alert, or run a task, when a counter crosses a defined threshold, which is what turns raw performance data into a proactive monitoring signal instead of a report someone has to read manually.

term: Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) and Data Collection Rules (DCR)
def: AMA is the unified agent installed on Azure VMs, Arc-enabled servers, or other machines to collect logs and performance data. A Data Collection Rule defines exactly what that agent collects, any transformation applied, and which Log Analytics workspace (or other destination) it is sent to.
prompt: _____ is the unified agent installed on Azure VMs, Arc-enabled servers, or other machines to collect logs and performance data. A Data Collection Rule defines exactly what that agent collects, any transformation applied, and which Log Analytics workspace (or other destination) it is sent to.
eg: AMA replaces the older Log Analytics (MMA/OMS) agent, and one DCR can be associated with many machines, which is what lets a single collection configuration apply consistently across a whole hybrid fleet.

term: Log Analytics workspace and Kusto Query Language (KQL)
def: A Log Analytics workspace is the container where Azure Monitor stores collected log data, queried using KQL, a read-only query language built around piping data through a chain of operators (like where, summarize, and project) to filter and shape results.
prompt: A Log Analytics workspace is the container where Azure Monitor stores collected log data, queried using _____, a read-only query language built around piping data through a chain of operators (like where, summarize, and project) to filter and shape results.
eg: Workspace-based queries also power log alert rules, so a KQL query that flags a problem interactively can usually be turned directly into an automated alert with very little extra work.

term: Azure Monitor alert rules and action groups
def: A metric alert evaluates a numeric signal (like CPU percentage) against a threshold on a schedule. A log alert runs a KQL query on a schedule and fires based on its results. An action group defines what happens when either fires — for example, an email, an SMS, a webhook, or an Azure Automation runbook.
eg: Separating the alert rule (the condition) from the action group (the response) means the same action group, say, paging the on-call team, can be reused across many different, unrelated alert rules.

term: Windows Admin Center monitoring and alerts
def: Windows Admin Center shows real-time and historical performance data for a managed server directly in the browser, and its Azure Monitor integration can connect that server to Azure Monitor from the same interface, so it can also feed Log Analytics-based alerting, without starting in the Azure portal.
eg: This lets an admin manage a purely on-premises server's health with the same tool used for day-to-day administration, while still optionally layering on Azure-based alerting for it.

def: Centrally assesses update compliance and schedules update installation across Azure VMs and Azure Arc-enabled on-premises (or other-cloud) servers from one place in the Azure portal, replacing the need to manage separate on-premises patching tools for those machines.
eg: A server must be Arc-enabled, or be a native Azure VM, before Update Manager can see or patch it at all — a plain on-premises server with no Arc agent and no Azure connection is invisible to it.

term: Reliability Monitor and Event Viewer for troubleshooting
def: Reliability Monitor plots a rolling stability index over time and correlates it with specific events (installs, crashes, updates), making it easy to spot when a problem started. Event Viewer provides the full, detailed event logs (System, Application, Security, and role-specific logs) needed to diagnose exactly what happened at that point.
eg: Reliability Monitor is a good first stop for figuring out when something started going wrong, after which Event Viewer's more detailed, filterable logs are what actually confirm the root cause.

def: WSUS is the traditional on-premises role for approving, staging, and distributing Windows updates to domain-joined clients and servers from local infrastructure, entirely independent of any Azure connection. It doesn't get replaced by Azure Update Manager the moment a server is Arc-enabled — the two can run side by side, and an Arc-enabled server shows compliance data in Update Manager only after an update assessment has run, whether on demand or through periodic assessment.

def: A built-in Windows feature that centralizes selected event log entries from many source servers onto one collector server, using a WinRM-based subscription — no Azure agent, Log Analytics workspace, or extra licensing required.
eg: WEF is the right call when a scenario rules out the Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules but still wants centralized Security/Application log review using only built-in Windows Server functionality.

term: VM insights and the dependency map
def: VM insights, built on the Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) and data collection rules (DCRs) plus a separate Dependency Agent, shows a server's running processes and the discovered connections and dependencies between servers — useful for migration planning and tracing a cross-server issue, across both Azure VMs and Arc-enabled on-premises servers. Microsoft has announced that the Map feature and the Dependency Agent retire on 30 June 2028 and should not be enabled for new deployments.
eg: The dependency map is what actually visualizes those discovered connections between machines — AMA alone collects logs and performance counters, but it's the separate Dependency Agent that supplies the process- and connection-level data the map is built from.

def: Best Practices Analyzer is a built-in Server Manager tool that scans an installed role, such as AD DS, DHCP, or Hyper-V, against Microsoft's own best-practice configuration rules for that specific role, flagging warnings and non-compliant settings directly in the console — a quick, role-specific health check that needs no Azure agent or external monitoring setup at all.

eg: BPA checks a role's own configuration against known-good practice; it doesn't track ongoing performance trends or correlate events the way Performance Monitor with Data Collector Sets, or Reliability Monitor with Event Viewer, does.

def: Change Tracking and Inventory records software, file, and registry changes made on a server over time, plus an inventory of its installed software and running services, so an administrator can correlate an incident with exactly what changed and when. It's delivered through the same Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) and Data Collection Rule (DCR) already used for other monitoring data, and works for both native Azure VMs and Azure Arc-enabled on-premises servers.

def: Azure's platform for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry. It gathers metrics and logs from Azure resources and, through Azure Arc and the Azure Monitor Agent, from on-premises servers, and it powers alerts, workbooks, VM insights, and the Log Analytics workspace.
prompt: Azure's platform for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry. It gathers metrics and logs from Azure resources and, through Azure Arc and the _____ Agent, from on-premises servers, and it powers alerts, workbooks, VM insights, and the Log Analytics workspace.
eg: For a Windows Server, the usual pattern is to Arc-enable it, install AMA, associate a data collection rule, then query or alert on the data in the workspace.

def: A cloud-native security information and event management (SIEM) and security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) service. It ingests security data from many sources into a Log Analytics workspace, detects threats with analytics rules, and responds with automation playbooks.
eg: Choose it when a scenario needs a unified security operations view across servers with custom detection and automated response. A Windows Event Forwarding collector alone gives collection, not detection.

def: The legacy Log Analytics agent, also called the OMS agent, that sent Windows server data to a Log Analytics workspace. It was retired on 31 August 2024 and replaced by the Azure Monitor Agent, which is configured with data collection rules.
eg: An option saying a server must 'run the legacy MMA first' is a distractor. For current designs use AMA, and servers outside Azure need Azure Arc to receive a data collection rule.

def: An Azure VM tool that collects and analyzes performance data, such as CPU, memory, disk, and network bottlenecks, and reports insights and recommendations. It can run on demand for an ongoing problem, or continuously on Windows VMs.
eg: For a VM with high CPU, the on-demand run from the VM's Performance diagnostics page gives deeper analysis than the charts alone. Results are stored in a storage account you choose.

def: A built-in Windows tool (resmon) that shows live CPU, memory, disk, and network use broken down by process, including which process holds a file handle or network port. It is a real-time view with no history.
eg: Use it to find the process behind a spike right now. Performance Monitor logs counters over time, and Reliability Monitor shows crashes and installs on a stability timeline.

def: System Insights, available on Windows Server 2019 and later, uses local machine learning to forecast resource consumption so problems are anticipated rather than reacted to. Four capabilities are on by default: CPU capacity forecasting, networking capacity forecasting per adapter, total storage consumption forecasting, and volume consumption forecasting. Everything runs locally with no cloud connection, and predictions are published to the event log and shown in Windows Admin Center or managed with PowerShell.
eg: Because results go to the event log, Azure Monitor or Operations Manager can collect and alert on them. It is predictive capacity planning, unlike Performance Monitor, which records what is happening now.

def: Windows Update writes trace files (.etl) that Get-WindowsUpdateLog merges into a readable WindowsUpdate.log, a static copy that is regenerated only when you run the cmdlet again. Work through the symptoms: confirm the update source (Microsoft Update, WSUS, or Azure Update Manager), connectivity to it, free disk space, and the Windows Update and BITS services, then review error codes such as 0x80070426 (ERROR_SERVICE_NOT_ACTIVE: a required service, for example the Microsoft Account Sign-in Assistant, is not running) and 0x8024402d (the update server is shedding load, so retry later), and repair components with DISM and sfc if the servicing stack is damaged.
eg: On Arc-enabled or Azure machines, Update Manager's assessment and installation history gives the first view. A firewall that blocks the BITS download path or a disabled Windows Defender Firewall service can both break downloads.

def: Work up the stack: confirm the adapter, address, gateway, and DNS servers (Get-NetIPConfiguration, ipconfig /all), test the specific service port with Test-NetConnection -ComputerName -Port (ping only tests ICMP), then test name resolution with Resolve-DnsName or nslookup against a chosen server, and clear stale answers with ipconfig /flushdns. Check firewall rules, NSGs, and whether the client uses the intended DNS server (a conditional forwarder or private resolver in hybrid setups).
eg: A name that resolves but a port that fails points to firewall or service trouble; a name that fails to resolve points to DNS, forwarders, or zone data. Compare the answer from the internal DNS server with the one from the Azure resolver when hybrid names disagree.

term: Troubleshooting disk encryption: Azure Disk Encryption and BitLocker
def: Azure Disk Encryption (ADE) encrypts VM OS and data disks inside the VM with BitLocker and keeps keys in Azure Key Vault. A failure such as 'Failed to send DiskEncryptionData' is usually caused by a Key Vault in a different region or subscription than the VM, access policies that do not allow ADE, a disabled or deleted key encryption key, a typo in the vault or key identifier, or blocked networking. ADE is scheduled for retirement on September 15, 2028, and encryption at host is recommended for new VMs.
eg: After that date ADE VMs keep running but encrypted disks will fail to unlock after a reboot, so migrate to encryption at host first. On-premises, BitLocker problems are resolved with the recovery password escrowed in Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID.
